_note: CONFIGURED REFERENCE DATA, NOT CODE. Run 101 section 12.3 fails the run for storing a revisable published industry figure as a literal in code, because it is revised annually and a literal cannot carry the year it belongs to. Every entry here carries its value, its unit, the year it describes, the source, and ITS VERIFICATION STATUS. Nothing in this file is a boundary the platform invented. THE TWO RESEARCH REPORTS THAT SUPPLY THESE FIGURES BOTH STATE THAT A PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION PASS WAS NOT COMPLETED, so every figure taken from them carries verified: false and names what must be checked. A reader can therefore say which numbers are locked and which still need checking against the source documents, which is the whole point of section 3's provenance requirement.

construction_industry_recordable_rate.unit: total recordable cases per 100 full-time equivalent workers, which is the same quantity as per 200,000 employee hours
construction_industry_recordable_rate.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Survey of Occupational Injuries and Illnesses (SOII), construction, NAICS 23, most recent published year 2023, as stated in RESEARCH_1_threshold_bands_eight_metrics.md and RESEARCH_2_safety_and_environmental_severity.md
construction_industry_recordable_rate.verification_note: BOTH RESEARCH REPORTS FLAG THIS VALUE [Confirm] AND STATE THAT PRIMARY-SOURCE VERIFICATION WAS NOT COMPLETED. Report 2's caveats say the exact current BLS rates must be checked against the named primary source and the current year before publication. It is stored as an UNVERIFIED published figure, not as a verified one.

companion_dart_rate.unit: days away, restricted or transferred cases per 100 full-time equivalent workers
companion_dart_rate.discrepancy_recorded: THE TWO RESEARCH REPORTS DISAGREE: one states approximately 1.4 and the other approximately 1.5. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved by picking one silently. No band is drawn on the DART rate, so the disagreement affects no reading today.

safety_exposure_floor_hours.unit: employee hours worked in the reporting period
safety_exposure_floor_hours.source: the owner's Run 101 order, section 3.6: 'Below roughly 200,000 hours a rate swings entirely on whether one event happened. State a floor in the specification and abstain beneath it.' 200,000 hours is also the OSHA normalising base itself, so beneath it the rate is an extrapolation from less than one base period.
safety_exposure_floor_hours.verification_note: RESEARCH_2 section 89 states explicitly: 'There is no OSHA/ANSI-published minimum-hours threshold.' The floor is therefore OWNER-CALIBRATED and is not presented as codified. 200,000 hours is about 100 worker-years and is the OSHA normalising base itself.

osha_severity_conventions.source: OSHA 29 CFR 1904 caps days away and restricted days at 180 each per case. The 6,000-day charge for death or permanent total disability is ANSI Z16.1's and is widely used. Both as stated in RESEARCH_2_safety_and_environmental_severity.md.
osha_severity_conventions.verification_note: RESEARCH_2 records that ANSI Z16.1 IS SUPERSEDED BY OSHA RECORDKEEPING IN US PRACTICE and that the current ANSI/ASSP designation should be verified. The 6,000-day charge is therefore a live convention whose standard citation is not confirmed.
osha_severity_conventions.no_severity_benchmark: RESEARCH_2: no published construction severity benchmark and no published good/average/bad severity cutoff exists. The severity rate therefore computes and displays and asserts NO band.

ilo_rate_base_hours.source: the owner's Run 101 order, section 3.6: international practice quotes rates on a 1,000,000-hour base, which differs from the OSHA 200,000-hour base by a factor of five.

cgp_corrective_action_deadline_days.source: EPA Construction General Permit, Part 5: corrective action before the next storm event where practicable and no later than 7 calendar days from discovery. Inspection frequency, about Part 4: every 7 calendar days, or every 14 days AND within 24 hours of a 0.25-inch storm event. Both as stated in RESEARCH_2_safety_and_environmental_severity.md.
cgp_corrective_action_deadline_days.verification_note: RESEARCH_2 marks the section numbers [Confirm section numbers against the 2022 CGP text]. The deadline itself is confirmed; the Part numbers are not.
cgp_corrective_action_deadline_days.no_published_severity_ladder: RESEARCH_2 section 142: 'no ready-made, citable construction environmental severity ladder exists. Construct one from statutory consequences and state plainly that the ordering is derived, not published.' ISO 14001 requires significance evaluation but prescribes no numeric scale.

rfi_contract_response_period_business_da.unit: business days, excluding weekends and holidays
rfi_contract_response_period_business_da.source: the owner's Run 101 order, section 4: the contract's own response period. A project whose contract states a different period overrides this, and the source is then that document.
rfi_contract_response_period_business_da.note: This is a DEFAULT standing in for a contract the platform has not read. Where a project supplies its own response period the project's figure governs.
rfi_contract_response_period_business_da.corroboration_recorded_not_used: Aboseif et al. (2023), Journal of Management in Engineering, derived from CII data by cross-validated CART models at 81 to 85 per cent accuracy, gives a high-performing RFI processing time of 7 days or fewer. THIS CORROBORATES THE PERIOD FROM AN EMPIRICAL DIRECTION AND IS NOT THE SOURCE: the owner's order is explicit that the basis is THE CONTRACT'S OWN RESPONSE PERIOD. The same paper's RFIs per million dollars figure measures a DIFFERENT QUANTITY and is not applied anywhere.

change_order_contingency_reserve_fractio.source: the owner's Run 101 order, section 4: a contingency reserve is conventionally around 20 per cent of contract value, so change exposure beyond 20 per cent has passed the money set aside to absorb it. Amber begins at half the reserve.

_provenance_of_this_file.how_obtained: The two research reports are the Run 101 order's section 0 authority for every number. THEY WERE NOT PRESENT IN THE REPOSITORY AND WERE NOT READ BY THIS RUN. Their figures reached this run RELAYED IN PROSE by the coordinating assistant mid-run, after goal one had first been implemented from the order's inline figures alone. The figures below are recorded as relayed and attributed to the named reports; no report file was opened.

construction_frequency_band_cutoffs.derivation: half the industry average, the industry average itself, and twice the industry average. All three are derived from the one anchor above and introduce no figure that is not already in it.
construction_frequency_band_cutoffs.source: the band shape recommended in RESEARCH_2_safety_and_environmental_severity.md: Green below about half the industry average (well-managed contractors commonly target below 1.0 to 1.5); Yellow at or below the BLS construction average; Amber above the industry average; Red at roughly twice the industry average or higher.
construction_frequency_band_cutoffs.why_not_codified: RESEARCH_2, recommendation 2, in terms: 'Band frequency against the published industry average, not an invented cutoff. State that ONLY THE INDUSTRY-AVERAGE ANCHOR IS SOURCED; intermediate cutoffs are platform-chosen with no published basis.' RESEARCH_1 section 5 more broadly: 'There is no recognized standard governing how a number maps to a Green/Yellow/Amber/Red band.' The ANCHOR is codified; these CUTOFFS are not, and the reading says so in both fields.

p80_gap_boundary.unit: fraction, gap = (P80 total cost - budget at completion) / budget at completion
p80_gap_boundary.source: RESEARCH_1_threshold_bands_eight_metrics.md sections 66 to 70 give the gap arithmetic: Green gap at or below 0; Yellow gap 0 to about +10 per cent; Amber about +10 to +20 per cent; Red above +20 per cent. THE OWNER'S ORDER'S ORDERING WINS where the two differ: the order puts Red at a budget below the median, not at a gap above 20 per cent, and that is what is implemented.
p80_gap_boundary.why_not_codified: RESEARCH_1 section 76 calls the exact gap boundaries 'moderate ... interpretive'. The P80 CONCEPT is codified -- DOE Order 413.3B and GAO-20-195G -- but this cutoff is not.

pert_criticality_bands.unit: criticality index = simulation runs in which the activity or path is critical / total simulation runs
pert_criticality_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 3, PERT Network Criticality.
pert_criticality_bands.hard_override: Red if the current deterministic schedule has zero or negative total float on the controlling path. The owner's stated rationale: zero total float defines a critical condition, while negative float indicates the current schedule cannot meet its imposed completion condition.
pert_criticality_bands.superseded_note: RUN 104. Retained as the record of what was measured before this run and NOT read by any module. The band was drawn over the criticality index of the MOST CRITICAL ACTIVITY, which on any network with a terminal milestone is critical in essentially every trial, so it banded Red on any valid network. High criticality of one path is not adverse; high uncertainty about which path controls is. See pert_path_concentration_bands.

pert_path_concentration_bands.unit: C1 = the probability of the most frequently critical PATH across the simulation trials, where the unit is the UNIQUE PATH and never a sum of activity criticality indices; M = C1 - C2, the dominance margin over the second most frequently critical path
pert_path_concentration_bands.source: the owner's Run 104 order, section 4. OWNER-CALIBRATED: the academic basis supports what a criticality index means; it does not prescribe these boundaries. They are a documented owner tolerance and are not presented as a construction standard.
pert_path_concentration_bands.hard_override: Red if the deterministic CPM forecast is later than an approved contractual milestone, or the controlling path has negative total float.

milestone_slip_ratio_bands.unit: slip ratio = (current forecast finish - approved baseline finish) / remaining planned duration
milestone_slip_ratio_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 3, Milestone Trend Analysis. The owner states in terms: 'The 2%, 5%, and 10% values are not universal construction standards; they are a documented owner tolerance structure that avoids treating a five-day slip identically on a 20-day package and a 1,000-day capital program.'
milestone_slip_ratio_bands.hard_override: Red if any contractual, regulatory, turnover or owner-committed milestone is forecast later than its approved date and no approved baseline change exists.

lookahead_readiness_bands.unit: constraint-free readiness = planned activities ready when due / planned activities due in the six-week window
lookahead_readiness_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 3, Look-Ahead Schedule Health. The owner's rationale: 'Look-ahead planning is specifically intended to identify and remove constraints before work is due.'
lookahead_readiness_bands.hard_override: Red if a critical-path or zero/negative-float activity is blocked by an unresolved constraint.

resource_peak_load_bands.unit: peak load ratio = peak planned resource demand / available planned resource capacity, for controlling and near-critical activities
resource_peak_load_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 3, Resource Loading Index. The owner's rationale: 'its actual risk depends on available capacity and the schedule consequence of the affected work.'
resource_peak_load_bands.hard_override: Red if any resource overload affects work on a zero or negative float path.
resource_peak_load_bands.no_conversion_between_unlike_resources: Unlike resources are NEVER aggregated into one ratio unless the project's resource plan defines a conversion. The ratio is formed per resource type in its own unit -- labour hours, crew-hours, equipment hours, or a named constrained resource -- and the peak across types is reported with the type named.

quality_first_pass_acceptance_bands.unit: first-pass inspection acceptance = items passing on first inspection / items inspected
quality_first_pass_acceptance_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 4.1.
quality_first_pass_acceptance_bands.not_sourced_to_rework_benchmarks: THE REWORK-COST BENCHMARKS MEASURE A DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- rework cost as a proportion of contract value -- and are NOT the source for these pass-rate bands. The owner states it in terms: 'Do not cite rework ratios as the source for these pass-rate bands.'
quality_first_pass_acceptance_bands.hard_override: Red if a critical inspection, hold-point inspection, life-safety requirement, commissioning acceptance test, or other explicitly designated critical quality item fails.

safety_benchmark_ratio_bands.unit: benchmark ratio = project TRIR / the applicable BLS construction TRIR
safety_benchmark_ratio_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 4.2. THE FORMULA AND THE BENCHMARK ARE CODIFIED; THE 0.75, 1.00 AND 1.50 MULTIPLIERS ARE OWNER-CONFIGURED. The benchmark itself is the separately configured entry 'construction_industry_recordable_rate' and is never written as a literal.
safety_benchmark_ratio_bands.hard_override: Red for a fatality, serious life-threatening event, stop-work order, or unresolved high-severity safety violation.
safety_benchmark_ratio_bands.display_rule: Total hours worked is always displayed beside the rate, because small projects can have volatile rates after a single recordable event. The exposure floor stays in force and nothing bands beneath it.

environmental_timely_closure_bands.unit: timely closure rate = corrective actions closed by their required deadline / corrective actions requiring closure
environmental_timely_closure_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 4.3. THE DEADLINE IS CODIFIED -- the project's permit, environmental management plan, or contract. THE PERCENTAGE BANDS ARE OWNER-CONFIGURED. The owner records that his research found no published universal aggregate closure-rate threshold.
environmental_timely_closure_bands.hard_override: Red for any overdue critical permit violation, enforcement notice, stop-work condition, or unclosed corrective action past a mandatory regulatory or permit deadline. A mandatory deadline ALWAYS overrides the percentage.

contractor_numeric_fallback_bands.unit: a numeric contractor performance score on a 0 to 100 scale
contractor_numeric_fallback_bands.source: the owner's Run 102 order and the threshold table and configuration-precedence appendix attached to it. OWNER-CONFIGURED: these are a documented owner tolerance structure, not a published construction standard. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them -- see the precedence order. Run 102 section 4.4. USED ONLY WHERE NO OWNER SCALE IS PROVIDED, and it yields to the contract's own scorecard or rating method.

critical_path_control_bands.unit: total float on the controlling path in working days on the approved project calendar; forecast completion slip in working days (current forecast finish minus approved baseline finish); and slip as a fraction of remaining planned working duration
critical_path_control_bands.worst_of: The final posture is the MOST SEVERE of four applicable results: the float band, the forecast-slip band, the percentage guardrail (a FLOOR, not a band: at least Yellow above 2 per cent, at least Amber above 5 per cent, Red above 10 per cent) and the milestone hard override.
critical_path_control_bands.hard_override: Red if any contractual, owner-committed, turnover or required milestone is forecast later than its approved baseline date, whatever the day count.
critical_path_control_bands.why_days_lead: Day bands lead and percentages guard. On a two-year project a 5 per cent slip is about 36 calendar days and 10 per cent about 73 -- far too late for an early warning. Fixed day bands give control sensitivity; the percentage keeps the rule sane on much shorter or much longer projects.
critical_path_control_bands.critical_and_near_critical_note: The critical-flag tolerance and the near-critical band are OWNER-CONFIGURED and are stated here rather than inferred. The tolerance is zero working days -- an activity is critical when its total float is at or below zero. The near-critical band is 10 working days, which is the owner's own Amber float band (1 to 10 days) and is used so that near-critical means the same thing as the band that would colour it Amber.
critical_path_control_bands.source: the owner's Run 103 order, sections 2.2, 2.3 and 3. OWNER-CONFIGURED CONSTRUCTION CONTROL TOLERANCE. These are NOT universal construction standards and are not presented as any: they are a documented owner tolerance. A stricter figure stated in a project document overrides them.

overhead_absorption_variance_bands.unit: overhead absorption variance = (actual overhead incurred - planned overhead absorbed) / planned overhead absorbed, as a fraction. A POSITIVE result is UNFAVOURABLE.
overhead_absorption_variance_bands.favourable_is_green: A favourable variance -- actual below planned -- is Green.
overhead_absorption_variance_bands.not_assessed: Not Assessed, never a posture, when planned absorbed overhead is zero or absent; when actual and planned cover different periods; or when the cost-code populations cannot be reconciled without a documented mapping. Never divide by zero and never infer a plan.
overhead_absorption_variance_bands.substantial_completion_floor: Where the project is substantially complete and final overhead remains materially unabsorbed, the posture is at least Amber, and Red above 15 per cent.
overhead_absorption_variance_bands.not_a_share_of_project_cost: This bands the VARIANCE against planned absorption for the same period and cost-code population. Absolute overhead as a share of project cost is a different quantity and is not banded here.
overhead_absorption_variance_bands.source: the owner's Run 103 order, section 4. OWNER-CONFIGURED COST VARIANCE TOLERANCE. These are NOT universal construction or regulatory thresholds and are not presented as any.
